deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page (fol. 17) restates Hilbert's 1888 theorem on definite forms and sums of squares. He phrases it as a question about rationally mapping the 'field' (open cone) of definite forms of degree m in n variables onto an unbounded Euclidean space by real rational, quadratic transformations. He notes this is possible for n=2 (m arbitrary), m=2 (n arbitrary) and n=3, m=4. He then asks how the other cases could be mapped.

(1) Continuation: 'Beispiel die binären Formen, die quadratischen Formen, die ternäre cubische Form f = x2^2 x3 + a x1^3 + b x1^2 x3 + c x1 x3^2 + d x3^3, wo alle Diskriminantenfälle rational erfüllt werden können.' The discriminant hypersurface splits coefficient space into open cells (the 'Diskriminantenfälle'), e.g. the number of real roots, or the signature. The claim is that for these families every such cell is the image of a real rational (indeed polynomial) map from a full parameter space. My reconstruction of why this holds:
- Binary forms of degree m: a form with k real linear factors and (m-k)/2 conjugate pairs is c * prod(x - r_i y) * prod((x - u_j y)^2 + v_j^2 y^2). Its coefficients are polynomials in the free real parameters c, r_i, u_j, v_j. These parameters run over all of R^N, and the image is the closed cell with that root configuration.
- Quadratic forms: f = sum_{i<=p} L_i^2 - sum_{p<i<=p+q} L_i^2 with real linear forms L_i. The coefficients of f are quadratic polynomials in the coefficients of the L_i, and this parametrizes all forms of signature (p,q) (rank <= p+q).
- The ternary cubic in Weierstrass-type normal form x2^2 x3 + g(x1,x3), with g a binary cubic: its real types (one oval branch or two branches) are governed by disc(g), whether g has 1 or 3 real roots. So this case reduces to binary cubics.

(2) 'Rationale Lösung der quadratischen Ungleichung f(x1..xn) >= 0 (<= 0)': find rational parametrizations whose image is exactly the solution set. Geometrically this is a rational map of a plane or space onto the interior of a conic or quadric. Example (mine): the closed unit disk 1-u^2-v^2 >= 0 is the image of R^2 under
u = 2w/(1+w^2) * (1-t^2)/(1+t^2), v = 2w/(1+w^2) * 2t/(1+t^2).
Indeed 1-u^2-v^2 = ((1-w^2)/(1+w^2))^2 >= 0, and conversely every point of the disk is attained. The same construction works for f >= 0 with f an indefinite quadratic form after diagonalization.

(3) Several simultaneous inequalities, e.g. the annulus between two circles, or the region between the two shells of a cyclide, are also to be mapped 'reell'. Example (mine), annulus 1 <= u^2+v^2 <= 4: radius rho = 1 + (2w/(1+w^2))^2 in [1,2], times the rational unit-circle point ((1-t^2)/(1+t^2), 2t/(1+t^2)). Hilbert's remark: solving inequalities is the algebraic meaning of the 'envelope' (Umhüllungs-) constructions of geometry.

(4) A methodological remark on definitions. A definition can never be 'false' nor illogical, being purely linguistic. It can only be unintelligible or ambiguous, and only then must it be discarded. Conflict with ordinary usage of the defined word is no essential defect.

(5) Start of a new topic, continued on fol. 19: the everywhere convergent power series y = sum_{n>=0} x^{n!}/((n!)!). Convergence for all x follows from the superexponential decay of the coefficients: ((n!)!)^{-1/n!} -> 0. On the next page Hilbert claims this entire function satisfies no algebraic differential equation G(x,y,...,y^(r)) = 0. His argument is a lacunarity argument: for n larger than the total degree s and the order r, the terms of the series must individually satisfy the reduced equation H.
errors: No computational errors on this page; the statements are programmatic.

The claim 'alle Diskriminantenfälle rational erfüllt' is asserted without proof. For the listed families it is true via root/signature parametrizations (my reconstruction), but Hilbert gives no argument here.

The hypertranscendence claim for sum x^{n!}/(n!)! is only stated here. The sketched proof on the next page ('each term separately satisfies H, hence every power and every polynomial does') is too quick as written. A rigorous version needs care with cross terms and with the possibility that H vanishes identically. The conclusion itself is true and follows from later gap theorems.

results.what: Rational/polynomial parametrization of each discriminant cell (real root configuration, signature) for binary forms, quadratic forms, and the Weierstrass-normal-form ternary cubic
results.modern_name: Rational (polynomial) parametrization of semialgebraic cells / real root-configuration strata
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (root and signature parametrizations, Sylvester's law of inertia); framed by Hilbert's 1888 work on nonnegative forms

results.what: Rational solution of quadratic inequalities: rational map of a plane/space onto the interior of a conic/quadric; several inequalities (annulus, region between shells of a cyclide)
results.modern_name: Images of polynomial/rational maps onto semialgebraic sets (cf. Fichou-Huisman-Mangolte-Monnier 'polynomial images'); connected to Hilbert's 17th problem (f >= 0 expressed rationally)
results.usually_credited_to: Systematic study of polynomial images of R^n: Gamboa, Ueno, Fernando et al. (1990s-2000s); positivity via squares: Hilbert 1888/1900, Artin 1927

results.what: A definition cannot be false or illogical, only unintelligible or ambiguous; deviation from common usage is harmless
results.usually_credited_to: Common view; Hilbert's later formalism (Grundlagen der Geometrie 1899, Frege correspondence)

results.what: The entire lacunary series y = sum x^{n!}/(n!)! satisfies no algebraic differential equation
results.usually_credited_to: Hölder 1887 (Gamma function); E. H. Moore 1896; gap-series results by Ostrowski, Popken, later Lipshitz-Rubel 1986 gap theorem; Hilbert mentioned hypertranscendence of sum x^n/n^s in the 1900 address

deep.surprise_reason: The forms/inequalities material is an informal extension of Hilbert's own 1888 program, an early hint at studying semialgebraic sets as rational images, but only programmatic. The definition remark foreshadows his known views. The most notable item is an explicit lacunary entire function asserted to be hypertranscendental, with a gap-type proof sketch, apparently c. 1888-1891. This predates Moore's 1896 paper and the gap-theorem literature. It is notable as an unpublished detail but not a major credited result.

checkable.asserts: The rational map lands in the closed unit disk: 1-u^2-v^2 is a perfect square
Discriminant equals (r1-r2)^2 (r1-r3)^2 (r2-r3)^2 >= 0, so the three-real-root cell is the polynomial image of R^3
Discriminant equals -4 v^2 ((r-u)^2+v^2)^2 <= 0, so the one-real-root cell is the polynomial image of R^3
The annulus parametrization radius rho in [1,2] gives 1 <= u^2+v^2 = rho^2 <= 4
Equals 0, i.e. the radius of convergence of sum x^(n!)/(n!)! is infinite (beständig convergent)
